text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- 250,000 people demonstration against the government's austerity programme. Protests in six cities. Trade unions criticise government as "capitalist stooges".
- Scarcely any improvement in east Germany's engineering sector.
- Doctors agree on new guidelines for medical charges.
- In Germany about one million people are employed in jobs connected with the environment.
HANDELSBLATT
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl said there was no power vacuum in Russia, after meeting President Boris Yeltsin for talks on Saturday.
- The Christian Democrats (CDU) say tax reform should come as a palpable relief. Finance Minister Theo Waigel expects upto 70 billion marks in new debt.
- German President Roman Herzog urged War World Two expellees to regard Germany as their home and called on Sudeten Germans to make their peace with Prague.
- German interest rates are in tune with economic fundamentals in Germany and the rest of Europe, according to Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer.
- Presumably more tax evasion in Germany than previously thought.
- Negotiations over a counter arrangement between the German Post and Postbank broke down.
- Social Democrat Rudolf Dressler warns that pensioners may not get pension rise in 1998.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- President Roman Herzog warns World War Two expellees from what was the Sudentenland that they have no claim to former eastern territories.
- DGB trade union federation demonstrations leave Bonn cold. Despite the big demonstrations the Bonn government is sticking to its austerity programme.

- Tax reform according to the Social Democrats would revive mass buying power. Lutz Hoffmann, the president of the German DIW economic research institute, says that a just tax scheme should be the main aim.
- German Bundestag lower house of parliament debates 1997 draft budget
DIE WELT
- Doctors want to place limits on their payments. Crisis meeting for federal association of doctors in Germany
- Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl dismissed DGB trade union federation's criticism of government. Finance Minister Theo Waigel expects more new public debt.
- Deutsche Bank may be fined. Investors withdraw 150 million pounds from investment funds.
- Investigations into Commerzbank management board.
